newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: King revokes call to release Cambodian prisoners.
newsitem.headline: King revokes call to release Cambodian prisoners.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk on Sunday reversed his call to release most of Cambodia's prisoners, stating that political opposition to the idea had led to his change of heart.

"I have no intention of having a political argument with anyone. So I would like to inform all my beloved people that today I withdraw my request for releasing prisoners," the king wrote in a statement released on Sunday, noting that politicians and university students alike had criticised his proposal.

Sihanouk, who proposed the mass amnesties in light of the recent pardoning of a leader from the genocidal 1975-1979 Khmer Rouge regime, faced mounting opposition from politicians angry at the prospect that the king might also pardon his half-brother, Prince Norodom Sirivudh, analysts said.
Sirivudh, who was exiled to France last year over an alleged plot to kill Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, had recently written to the king asking for permission to return home.
Newspapers affiliated with Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party launched stong attacks on the mass amnesty plan.
In proposing the mass amnesty, Sihanouk noted the pardon given to dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary and said others who had committed far lesser crimes than the Khmer Rouge should be forgiven.
The Khmer Rouge are blamed for the deaths of more than one million Cambodians during their brutal regime of the late 1970s.
